Huberman, Ph.D.","uri":"https://x.com/hubermanlab"},"published":"2026-11-21T20:33:25.000Z","references":[{"relation":"repost","id":"x:tweet:2124216644046340591","link":"https://x.com/HLPClips/status/2124216644046340591","item":{"id":"x:tweet:2124216644046340591","title":"If you're not frustrated you're not learning:","link":"https://x.com/HLPClips/status/2124216644046340591","description":"If you're not frustrated you're not learning:

Errors are what generate plasticity. The reaches and failures signal to the nervous system that this isn't working, so the circuitry starts to shift.

The brain doesn't understand frustration as an emotional state. It understands the neurochemicals errors release: epinephrine and acetylcholine, then dopamine once you start approximating the right behavior.

The few people who can stay in that feeling do exceedingly well. The ones who can't generally don't learn much.

Errors plus corrective feedback drive learning; frustration itself isn't required, and heavy frustration can hurt performance.
